verdict: Caution: lend selectively to domestic-focused Bahadurgarh footwear units with clean receivables; avoid export-dependent leather shoe makers until West Asia demand recovers.
title: Bahadurgarh Footwear: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Bahadurgarh footwear is a low-capex, labour-heavy assembly business where cash sits in inventory and receivables, not in plant.** Units buy leather, soles and synthetics, cut and stitch, and sell either to domestic wholesalers or export to West Asia. Entry barriers are low because the process is not capital-intensive [10], so pricing power is thin and the unorganised sector sets the floor. **When a proposal lands, check whether the borrower sells domestic or export; if export-heavy, ask for the buyer-wise order book and shipping bills.**

## What has broken now
**The local shock is export-side: one Bahadurgarh leather shoe factory reports exports down 50% due to the West Asia war [1].** Separately, Rohtak-Bahadurgarh industries are buckling under rising costs and labour migration [3]. Nationally, exports are -3.0% Apr-to-date in USD [D], which matches the local export pain. **So when a proposal lands, check export share of revenue; if above 30%, ask for the last six months of buyer-wise dispatches and any order cancellations.**

## Where the growth is
**The domestic side is the opportunity: Haryana GST collections are +10.1% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% [D], and India-wide footwear output (IIP NIC 15) is +8.1% YoY [D].** Peer results confirm domestic demand is real: Relaxo Q4 FY26 revenue grew 8.1% YoY to INR751 crore with EBITDA margin 16.5% [5], and Bata India Q1FY27 net profit rose 23% YoY to Rs 64 crore [6]. **Take a covenant that export receivables above 30% of sales require ECGC cover or a buyer-wise collection report.** The sector needs plant and machinery investment to grow [11], so capex loans should be matched to confirmed orders, not optimism. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch labour migration and power/LPG cost chatter in local press [3]; if a borrower reports worker shortage or a shift cut, ask for the monthly production register.** Watch GST filing gaps; if two consecutive months slip, ask for the sales register and bank statements.
watch: Two consecutive late filings -> ask for sales register and bank statements, freeze limit enhancement
Above 30% without ECGC cover -> require buyer-wise collection report or reduce exposure
Reported shift cut or worker shortage -> ask for monthly production and dispatch data
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
